A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GOAT research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial changes in presentation and experimental coverage.

before.justification: v3 reports original cooperative matrix game experiments, Overcooked simulations, a 40-participant human study, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v4 reports original CMG and Overcooked results, the human study, and newly added Cooperative Reaching Game evaluations against 11 heuristic partners.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same procedure: a frozen VAE generates partners from adversarial embeddings, self-play minus cross-play defines regret, and the adversary and cooperator train online. PPO and REINFORCE remain the respective training algorithms. Revised hyperparameters and omitted implementation disclosures do not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: v4 adds Cooperative Reaching Game, a 5-by-5 environment requiring simultaneous arrival at shared goals, evaluated against 11 heuristic partners. Its stated Overcooked coverage narrows from six layouts to Counter Circuit and Multi-Strategy Counter, and the earlier across-layout aggregate disappears. CMG-M and appendix CMG-S remain.

E2.justification: The CMG-M comparison adds GAMMA and Minimax and removes TrajeDi (v3 Figure 3 versus v4 Figure 2). TrajeDi remains in CMG-S. The five Overcooked baselines remain unchanged; shortened BC and GAMMA figure labels correspond to BC+RL and MEP+GAMMA in the baseline descriptions.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes the reported adversary learning rate from 0.001 to 0.0005 and KL coefficient from 0.1 to 5.0. v4 also introduces CMG expected-reward evaluation under uniformly sampled partners and the CRG evaluation protocol. The human study retains 40 participants, six rounds, and randomized agent order. These reported revisions do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 extends the regret-versus-minimax ablation to CMG-M and removes the supplementary human-rating analyses in v3 Appendix J. The Overcooked minimax ablation, latent-space exploration analysis, VAE reconstruction/interpolation demonstrations, and CMG-S analysis remain, several under reordered appendix labels.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix G/Table 4 reports ten human-performance t-tests with a Bonferroni threshold of 0.005. v4 removes this entire inferential analysis without replacement. Five-seed standard-error reporting for the Overcooked learning curves remains, but the human comparisons lose their explicit statistical testing.

E6.justification: The Counter Circuit human results reverse GOAT's ranking relative to GAMMA: GOAT is lower in v3 Figure 5 and higher in v4 Figure 4c, with v4 describing a 3% lead. The Counter Circuit GOAT learning curve also changes. v4 adds CMG expected rewards and CRG results, including score sums of 9.70 for GOAT and 9.40 for GAMMA, while removing the across-layout aggregate and human-rating results. These are reported result changes, not established controlled performance gains.

T1.justification: The Markov-game formulation, minimax objectives, and self-play-minus-cross-play regret definition remain substantively unchanged. v4 makes the generated partner's dependence on the adversary explicit and shortens the ELBO/self-play exposition, including removing the displayed standard ELBO formula. No substantive mathematical assumption, theorem, proof, or derivation changes.

C1.justification: The central claims about frozen generative partners, online regret-driven curricula, and human coordination remain. The introduction adds an explicit contribution claiming superiority over five baselines across three environments, and the conclusion broadens its empirical scope accordingly. This expands the performance claim without redefining the methodological contribution.

C2.justification: v4 drops v3's explicit qualification that Counter Circuit human performance is not significantly different from GAMMA, instead discussing a small advantage and stating the near-optimal-performance explanation more definitively. It also revises the minimax failure description toward unproductive but nonsabotaging behavior. The limitation concerning VAE training quality and sufficient data remains.

D1.justification: v4 omits generator entropy, scaling, clipping, scheduler settings, and the hard-bound description, while adding definitions of the 11 CRG heuristics. Reported compute changes from approximately 3600 GPU hours to 24–36 for Overcooked and one hour for other environments, without clarifying comparable accounting. Specific CMG Colab guidance is removed, although the project webpage and code disclosure remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds relevant UED and teamwork references, including Jiang et al. (2021), Parker-Holder et al. (2022), RACCOON, ROTATE, and Villin et al. (2025), and removes the Bonferroni reference. It gives minimax approaches a separate discussion while retaining the existing positioning around frozen generative partners and online rather than population-pretraining adversarial optimization.

P1.justification: v4 condenses and rewrites portions of the introduction, related work, method explanation, and results discussion. It consolidates experimental subsections into environment bullets and run-in headings, reorders appendices, and switches citation style. The main section sequence and five research-question narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v4 substantially reorganizes the visual presentation: CMG gains an expanded comparison grid and reward chart; CRG gains result and environment figures; and Overcooked layouts, learning curves, and human scores are consolidated into Figure 4. The across-layout summary, significance table, and human-rating panels disappear. Other appendix figures are retained and relocated, alongside a document-wide template change.

improvement.justification: The CRG evaluation and expanded CMG comparisons strengthen empirical coverage, and the consolidated Overcooked figure helps comparison. However, v4 removes the human significance tests and several reproduction details while replacing Counter Circuit results and broadening performance claims. The PDFs leave a material tradeoff between stronger coverage and reduced statistical and implementation transparency, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
